risk_if_not_implemented: Without Prohibited Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS), Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS) may operate with insecure, unauthorized or drifted configurations that expand the attack surface. Based on the risk and threat mapping for this control, this deficiency most likely exposes the organization to Regulatory / Legal / Contractual Financial Liability (R-EX-5), Uncontrolled Third-Party Security / Privacy Exposure (R-GV-5), Third-Party Cybersecurity Compromise / Exposure (R-SC-1), Third-Party Legal / Compliance Exposure (R-SC-4), and most likely increases susceptibility to Human Error (MT-9), Statutory / Regulatory / Contractual Change (MT-11), Foreign Ownership, Control, or Influence (FOCI) (MT-17), Sanctions / Trade Restriction Disruption (MT-19).

compensating_control_1.name: Software Usage Restrictions
compensating_control_1.description: Mechanisms exist to enforce software usage restrictions to comply with applicable contract agreements and copyright laws.
compensating_control_1.justification: Software Usage Restrictions (CFG-11) provides overlapping security capability that compensates for the absence of Prohibited Equipment & Services (AST-12) by addressing related risk objectives through an alternative control mechanism aligned with Process applicability. Given the process-oriented nature of this control, this compensating control targets the same underlying risk objective through an alternative approach, helping to maintain an acceptable level of residual risk until the primary control can be implemented.

compensating_control_2.name: Boundary Protection
compensating_control_2.description: Mechanisms exist to monitor and control communications at the external network boundary and at key internal boundaries within the network.
compensating_control_2.justification: Boundary Protection (NET-03) provides network-level access restriction that compensates for the absence of Prohibited Equipment & Services (AST-12) by limiting attacker reach and lateral movement opportunities across the environment. Given the process-oriented nature of this control, this compensating control targets the same underlying risk objective through an alternative approach, helping to maintain an acceptable level of residual risk until the primary control can be implemented.
